Mesh processing

Source: R/mesh-processing.R
mesh_processing.Rd

Verbs on a mesh_3d() corner table (also an rgl mesh3d or any data frame with x, y, z, .face, .corner and .vertex, optionally split into parts by .mesh). They work on one half-edge representation of each part: polygon faces are triangulated (quads along the shorter diagonal), faces with a repeated corner are dropped, faces are wound consistently within each connected component (with a warning when some had to be reversed), and a vertex where several fans of faces meet only at a point is split into one vertex per fan. An edge shared by more than two faces, or a non-orientable surface, is an error.

Usage

mesh_normals(m, crease = 30)

mesh_curvature(m)

mesh_subdivide(m, n = 1L, scheme = c("loop", "midpoint"))

mesh_smooth(m, iterations = 10L, lambda = 0.5, mu = -0.53)

mesh_decimate(m, target = 0.5, max_error = Inf, boundary_weight = 100)

mesh_remesh(m, edge = NULL, iterations = 10L)

Arguments

m

A mesh: a mesh_3d() corner table or a compatible data frame.

crease

Dihedral angle in degrees above which an edge splits the normals of its vertices.

n

Number of subdivision rounds.

scheme

"loop" or "midpoint".

iterations

Number of smoothing or remeshing iterations.

lambda, mu

Taubin step factors, lambda > 0 > mu.

target

Number of faces to keep, or a fraction of the triangle count.

max_error

Largest root mean squared distance a collapse may cause, in the units of the positions.

boundary_weight

Weight of the planes that hold boundary edges.

edge

Target edge length; NULL uses the mean edge length.

Value

A mesh of the class of m.

Details

mesh_normals() sets nx, ny, nz per corner to the angle-weighted mean of the face normals around the vertex (Thuermer and Wuethrich 1998), taken separately on each side of an edge whose faces meet at more than crease degrees and of a boundary edge; crease = 180 gives one smooth normal per vertex.

mesh_curvature() adds gaussian_curvature (angle defect over the mixed Voronoi area) and mean_curvature (half the norm of the cotangent Laplacian) at every vertex (Meyer et al. 2003). Mean curvature is signed against the vertex normal of the face winding, negative where the surface bends away from its normal, so a sphere wound outwards has mean curvature -1/r, as in stat_parametric_3d(). Boundary vertices are NA.

mesh_subdivide() splits every triangle into four, n times. "loop" places the points with Loop's (1987) masks, approximating a smooth surface; boundary curves follow the cubic B-spline rule. "midpoint" keeps the triangles' planes.

mesh_smooth() runs Taubin's (1995) lambda/mu smoothing: each iteration moves every interior vertex by lambda and then by mu times the vector to the mean of its neighbours; mu < -lambda stops the shrinking of plain Laplacian smoothing. Boundary vertices stay fixed.

mesh_decimate() collapses edges by the quadric error metric of Garland and Heckbert (1997) until the mesh has target faces (a fraction of the triangle count when below one) or the next collapse would move the surface by more than max_error. Vertex quadrics sum the planes of their faces weighted by area; the error of a collapse is the area-weighted root mean squared distance of the merged vertex from these planes, at the position that minimises it (with directions of small curvature truncated, as in Lindstrom 2000). Boundary edges add perpendicular planes weighted by boundary_weight times their squared length. A collapse is refused when it would make the surface non-manifold or turn a face normal by more than 90 degrees.

mesh_remesh() makes edges close to length edge by the isotropic remeshing of Botsch and Kobbelt (2004): split edges longer than 4/3 edge, collapse edges shorter than 4/5 edge, flip edges towards valence six, relax vertices tangentially and project them back onto the input surface. Boundary vertices are kept.

Rebuilding verbs (all but mesh_normals() and mesh_curvature()) carry attributes over: double columns constant per vertex are interpolated, other vertex columns follow the vertex each new vertex derives from, and columns constant per face follow the input face each new face lies in. When the input has normals or curvature, they are recomputed.

References

Thuermer and Wuethrich (1998). Computing vertex normals from polygonal facets. Journal of Graphics Tools 3, 43-46. doi:10.1080/10867651.1998.10487487

Meyer, Desbrun, Schroeder and Barr (2003). Discrete differential-geometry operators for triangulated 2-manifolds. Visualization and Mathematics III, 35-57. doi:10.1007/978-3-662-05105-4_2

Loop (1987). Smooth subdivision surfaces based on triangles. MSc thesis, University of Utah. https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/smooth-subdivision-surfaces-based-on-triangles/

Taubin (1995). A signal processing approach to fair surface design. SIGGRAPH '95, 351-358. doi:10.1145/218380.218473

Garland and Heckbert (1997). Surface simplification using quadric error metrics. SIGGRAPH '97, 209-216. doi:10.1145/258734.258849

Lindstrom (2000). Out-of-core simplification of large polygonal models. SIGGRAPH 2000, 259-262. doi:10.1145/344779.344912

Botsch and Kobbelt (2004). A remeshing approach to multiresolution modeling. Symposium on Geometry Processing, 185-192. doi:10.2312/SGP/SGP04/189-196

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 12),
                 y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 12), z = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 12))
d$value <- with(d, x^2 + y^2 + z^2)
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, value = value))
sphere <- ggplot2::layer_data(p + stat_isosurface_3d(levels = 0.6) + coord_3d())
sphere <- sphere[c("x", "y", "z", ".face", ".corner", ".vertex")]
coarse <- mesh_decimate(sphere, 0.25)
smooth <- mesh_smooth(mesh_subdivide(coarse), iterations = 5)
curved <- mesh_curvature(smooth)
summary(curved$mean_curvature)
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  geom_mesh_3d(data = curved, ggplot2::aes(fill = mean_curvature)) + coord_3d()
